# GEO report: atlas-roadmaps

**New to GEO?** GEO (generative engine optimization) means making your site easy for search engines and AI tools to find, read and quote. This report checks the technical basics.

## Code score: 40/100, At risk

Confidence: High (checked 23 of 23 points).
How it's calculated: low = 16.08 ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. High = (16.08 + 0) ÷ 23 × 100 = 70. Both are capped at 40 because of a blocker: Bingbot is blocked from the whole site, which goes against your declared policy of allowing AI search crawlers (GEO-009).

Without the cap, the score would be 70. Nothing was left unknown, so the code decides every result. These results are read from code, not measured on a live site.

## Live check

- **Not run.** To add it, give me your site's URL.

## Do these first

### 1. Let Bingbot crawl the site
- **Why it matters:** Bing powers search results in several AI tools. Blocking it contradicts your `aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"` policy and caps the score.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:5-6`
- **What the code says:** `User-agent: Bingbot` / `Disallow: /`
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** 83/100, Good. The cap is removed and GEO-009 earns its full 3 points.

### 2. Point robots.txt at the sitemap
- **Why it matters:** Crawlers find the sitemap faster when robots.txt links to it.
- **Where:** `public/robots.txt:9`. The file ends with no `Sitemap:` line.
- **What the code says:** `Disallow: /` (last line, no `Sitemap:` anywhere)
- **Size:** Small
- **Score after this:** alone it is still 40 because of the cap. Together with item 1 it is 91, Strong.

### 3. Render the changelog on the server
- **Why it matters:** Entries are fetched in the browser after load, so crawlers that don't run JavaScript see an empty list.
- **Where:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5`
- **What the code says:** `useEffect(() => { fetch('/api/changelog')…`
- **Size:** Medium. Move the fetch into a Remix `loader`.
- **Score after this:** alone it is still 40 because of the cap. Together with items 1 and 2 it is 94.

## All results

| Rule | What it checks | Code | Where |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GEO-013 | robots.txt valid | Clear | `public/robots.txt` is plain text with valid lines |
| GEO-009 | Search crawlers allowed | Problem | `public/robots.txt:5-6` blocks Bingbot site-wide (a blocker). GPTBot is blocked, which matches your training policy and isn't counted. |
| GEO-014 | Routes indexable | Clear | 4 routes checked, no noindex. `/dashboard` is noindex and not in the sitemap, which looks deliberate. |
| GEO-015 | Absolute canonical | Problem | `/pricing` has none (`app/routes/pricing.tsx`). 3 of 4 routes are clear. |
| GEO-003 | Content in server HTML | Problem | `app/routes/changelog.tsx:5`. 3 of 4 routes are clear. |
| GEO-004 | JSON-LD valid | Not applicable | No JSON-LD found |
| GEO-011 | Sitemap discoverable | Problem | `public/sitemap.xml` is valid, but robots.txt has no `Sitemap:` line |
| GEO-012 | Title, description, lang | Clear | `app/root.tsx:2,5`. `/pricing` falls back to the root defaults. |
| GEO-016 | Server-rendered links | Problem | `/features` is reached only by `onClick` (`app/routes/_index.tsx:9`). 2 of 3 routes are clear. |
| GEO-017 | No snippet blocking | Clear | No `nosnippet` found in the 5 route files |
| GEO-002 | Accessibility basics | Clear | Read `app/root.tsx` and all 5 routes. No images, and `<main>` and `<h1>` are present. |
| GEO-101 | App association files | Not applicable | No mobile app declared |
| GEO-010 | llms.txt (info) | Not scored | Not present |
| GEO-102 | App structured data (info) | Not scored | Not present |

## Other problems found

- **Click-only link:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:9`: `<div onClick={() => navigate('/features')}>`. Use `<Link to="/features">`. This is the same issue as GEO-016.

## Worth considering

- **Back up the integrations claim:** `app/routes/_index.tsx:8`: `Integrates with all the tools you already use.` Name the actual integrations, with a link or list.
- **Pricing page has no prices:** `app/routes/pricing.tsx:1`: `Talk to us for a quote.` Show plan names, tiers or price ranges as text. Visitors come to this page for that.
- **Give /pricing its own title and description:** it currently shows the root's `Atlas` and `Roadmaps your whole team can follow.` (`app/root.tsx:2`).
- **Link Features from the main navigation:** `app/root.tsx:7` lists only Pricing and Changelog.
- **Add `<lastmod>` to the sitemap:** `public/sitemap.xml:3-6` has none. Changelog dates would be a natural source.
- **Date the changelog entries and give each its own page:** `app/routes/changelog.tsx:6` renders bare `<li>` strings.
- **Add Organization or WebSite JSON-LD:** nothing in the code states the site's name or URL in a machine-readable way. The root layout is where it would go.
- **Add `charset` and `viewport` meta:** `app/root.tsx:2` doesn't set them.
- **Expand the Features page:** `app/routes/features.tsx:1` promises "Timelines, sharing and status updates" in one sentence. A short section on each would give readers something to quote.

## Can't tell from code

- **Bot protection:** code can't show whether a CDN or firewall lets real crawlers through. Run `geopilot logs <access log>` to check real crawlers against their published addresses.
- **`/api/changelog`:** no route for it exists in the repo, so its behaviour is unknown.

## Assumptions

- You want AI search tools to find this site, which matches `policy.aiSearchCrawlers: "allow"`.
- `/dashboard` is private on purpose, so it was left out of the route sample.

## What to do next

1. Run the geopilot `fix` command to apply item 1. You'll see every change before anything is written.
2. Run the geopilot `explain` command with any rule id, such as `GEO-009`, to learn more.
3. For proof from a running site, ask for a live scan with its URL.

Technical readiness only. GEO does not measure or predict citations, rankings, traffic or inclusion in any AI or search product.
